QuestionText: Which command sets your Git username?
Explanation: Use git config user.name to set your Git username.

QuestionText: What does --global mean in git config?
OptionA: Sets config only for this repo
OptionB: Applies to all repositories on the system
Explanation: Applies to all repositories on the system.

QuestionText: Which command displays all Git config settings?
Explanation: git config --list shows all Git configuration settings.

QuestionText: Where is global Git config stored?
Explanation: Global config is stored in the user’s home directory in ~/.gitconfig.

QuestionText: What file contains repository-specific Git config?
Explanation: Local config for a repo is saved in .git/config within that repo.

QuestionText: How do you set your Git email globally?
Explanation: Use git config --global user.email to set a global email.

QuestionText: Which Git command sets the default text editor?
Explanation: You can set the editor using git config core.editor.

QuestionText: Which config scope overrides others?
Explanation: Local settings override global and system configs.

QuestionText: Which command removes a Git config entry?
Explanation: Use git config --unset to delete a config entry.

QuestionText: What does git config credential.helper store do?
Explanation: It stores credentials securely so you don't have to re-enter them.

QuestionText: What is the purpose of git config?
OptionB: To configure Git settings like username, editor
Explanation: git config is used to customize Git behavior and set user preferences.

QuestionText: Which flag do you use with git config for repo-specific settings?
Explanation: Use --local to apply configuration to the current repository only.

QuestionText: How can you set a default merge tool in Git?
Explanation: You can set the default merge tool using git config merge.tool <tool>.

QuestionText: What does git config --global core.autocrlf true do?
OptionB: Normalizes line endings to CRLF on checkout
OptionD: Normalizes line endings to CRLF on checkout
Explanation: This setting converts LF to CRLF on checkout to handle line endings.

QuestionText: Which command sets the default push behavior?
Explanation: git config push.default can control push behavior like matching or simple.

QuestionText: What is the purpose of git config user.signingkey?
OptionB: Sets GPG signing key for commits
OptionD: Sets GPG signing key for commits
Explanation: You can configure a GPG key for signing commits using this setting.

QuestionText: How do you view system-wide Git config?
Explanation: git config --system --list shows system-level configuration.

QuestionText: Where is the system Git config usually located?
Explanation: System-wide Git config is typically located in /etc/gitconfig.

QuestionText: What happens if the same config key is in system, global, and local?
Explanation: Local config has the highest priority, overriding global and system values.

QuestionText: Which command sets an alias in Git?
Explanation: You can set command aliases using git config alias.<command>=<actual command>.
